title: Oneshots
author: PeanutSilent884
selftext: I might be an outlier but I kind of like seeing these one shot posts, granted my favourite bit is seeing them get thrashed in the comments. But how long do you think ,if ever, it will take before a game can be made in say less than a year using ai? Will the models we use today be so obsolete in a year that what takes six months now could be done in a week at some point ?

comments.author: mugwumps
comments.body: hahaha seeing all the crybabies is the best part. Just embrace technology

comments.author: ChocolateTemporary48
comments.body:
Siendo sinceros, si buscas juegos simples ya se pueden hacer en unas pocas horas, no en un one shot, pero si bastante rápido siempre y cuando tengas los promts correctos.

No serán perfectos y todo depende mucho del modelo que uses, pero al menos funcionan.


En un año lo más probable es que veamos un aumento masivo en la calidad, pero seguirá sin haber one shots decentes, simplemente porque la IA tiene demasiadas opiniones raras preparadas y hay que ajustarlas.

replies.author: SpaghettiMan247
replies.body: Yeah, the only way we are getting a really good one shot anytime soon is a combination of #1 stronger models and #2 somebody writes a literal book length single prompt.

replies.author: ChocolateTemporary48
replies.body:
Tener en cuenta cada detalle y un modelo potente, de lo contrario salen cosas muy raras o limitadas.

Sin mencionar las muchas pruebas que tienes que hacer después.

Ajustes de arquitectura, y todo eso.

comments.author: -Unpaid_Wizard-
comments.body: I started my game with a one shot prompt then cleaned up the code and built it out from there. I am now 5 days in and this thing is looking really fucking good.

comments.author: sirpalee
comments.body: You can already make a game in months with the current models. Just not one shot it.

replies.author: PeanutSilent884
replies.body: I mean a real game , not some 1 level 2d platformer trash

replies.author: sirpalee
replies.body: A real game, yes. Smaller indie game, but you can definitely make one with the current models. You just know what to do and not aimlessly prompt.

replies.author: thetinytrex
replies.body: You can absolutely make a game and arguably in one shot, but the vast majority do not understand game design and misconstrue what constitutes as a game. If you think only AAA 200+ hour story campaign is the only bar for being called a "game" then your definition is delusional. Most of these one shots are indeed demos and have scopes way beyond what can be done in a one shot. But small games exist. Micro games exist.

replies.author: Stock_Restaurant3791
replies.body: Lmao ik what post ur referencing

replies.author: kytheon
replies.body: You can make a "real game" today and publish it. Just not a one shot.

comments.author: Backroadsgaming
comments.body:
depending on the amount of $$$ you want to spend, you can actually have a decent working Prototype of a full fledged survival RPG in a weekend.

Biggest issues I have seen come from the art.

For example Tripo--if you reduce the tris count down, the art comes out very deformed but to get the clean topo on it, you have to use a stupid high tris count which would only work good for a "hero" character or object (something that is not mass populated in the game)

So yes its doable but all depends on how you want it looking.

replies.author: PeanutSilent884
replies.body: I guess i am thinking beyond prototype , and we are spending quite a bit already on these models ! Agreed on art ..and sound but I  think a lot of modern ish unreal games lean onto realism more than art (i am not saying art is not a factor, but I hope you know what I mean) . But i personally think an indie developer with experience in game dev(that's not me) who knows the materials and methods could potentially with the help of all the AI tools we have now could potentially create an almost AAA game

replies.author: Backroadsgaming
replies.body:
no absolutely, I agree... if someone takes the time, they can do a TON above and beyond what AI starts with.

For example..  Tripo can make a GREAT model, but the tris count is way to high, so the dev takes said model into blender, reduces the tris count, and then redoes the UV Mapping.. and then from there they tweak the materials, enhancing the existing material and then making it even better (possibly realistic)

I think thats what sets Idie Devs apart from those that just pump out 100 Reskinned games with little or no work other that... Chatgpt make this game for me.

(I currently am using AI to generate a lot of the code an art I am using in a Mobile game i am currently developing.. some of it worked out of the gate (the art stuff works pretty decent becuase its all 2d stuff) but I had to do a good bit of code adjustment, and re-iterations on certain parts of the artwork because of scaling, or similarity ( ie. make a raccoon running sprite sheet, and it gives me the sprite sheet with the animations but every animation the raccoon looked different either scale/color/number of feeet lol)

AI is here to stay, its not going away anytime soon, and it does open the door for a lot of people who would have otherwise never considered making their own game, but with the tools that make life easier, there are those who will mis-use or not use with the original intent.

comments.author: Odd_While7691
comments.body: I think they are useful. It's a solid gauge at where the models are at the very least. Imagine trying to do all this w GPT3. The one shots will be better next generation as well. Its fun to watch the progression.

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
you really should be thinking in terms of usage/token instead of simply time spent. 

in 2026, you can make a big game in weeks if you are burning usage/tokens 24/7. 

the "rules" for one-prompt is basically that they don't prompt again so whatever the usage/token count is after the one prompt is their final usage/token count. 

those posts are benchmarking exercises + memes (some people do it for the memes but a typical one-prompter usually does provide the technical info for reference)

comments.author: BlueAndYellowTowels
comments.body:
Right now, you have everything you need to make a game as a non-developer. A couple subscriptions and you could be well on your way.

I think, there will always be a "minimum time" because games aren't just about the technical side. 

Like, if you're making an RPG. You have to write a story, have compelling characters and themes. You need to think of a setting and themes... and the list goes on and on... even if everything is automated away from the technical side you still have the "RPG Maker" problem in that... you actually have to have something compelling that people want to play.

comments.author: GlobalCurry
comments.body: You can kind of one shot now if you use goals in codex and provide a document with most of the plan laid out already and just let it burn through tokens. Your plan has to be detailed though and token usage will be high.
